Summary assessment with SLOOS context:
- The April 29, 2020 FOMC statement is distinctly negative on growth, employment, and inflation, committing to the effective lower bound and open-ended asset purchases to support market functioning and credit flows.
- The April 2020 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) corroborates and amplifies the downside tone: banks and foreign banks reported broad-based tightening in C&I lending (including to middle-market firms), CRE (nonfarm nonresidential, construction/land development, multifamily), and HELOCs; widened loan-rate spreads and higher costs on credit lines; tighter LTVs and other terms; and expectations of further tightening. Reported drivers include COVID-19, a deteriorating economic outlook, industry-specific problems, reduced risk tolerance, and liquidity needs. Demand weakened notably in CRE, with only pockets of strength in government-backed residential mortgages.
- These SLOOS findings validate the statement’s concern about impaired credit flows and imply persistent credit headwinds to the real economy despite improved market functioning from policy backstops.

Net effect: Policy support is strong, but the SLOOS evidence of tighter lending standards and weaker credit demand deepens the negative assessment versus using the FOMC statement alone (or even the FSR). Therefore, sentiment is adjusted modestly more negative.

sentiment score = -0.62
